builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
summary: It replaces parametric memory training and unbounded append-and-search history stores with six typed memory agents holding complete records, a provenance hypergraph index, and retrieval under explicit evidence budgets. It costs the operational complexity of running multiple memory agents plus an offline consolidation process (AutoDream), and requires no fine-tuning, working with closed or open models behind APIs. It can fail if the provenance index or retrieval budgets drop relevant records on the reader's specific workloads, since reported gains come from public QA and embodied-task benchmarks that may not transfer.
rationale: The system needs no training and runs against API-hosted models, fitting constrained infrastructure, but its accuracy and latency advantages are benchmark-specific and must be validated on the reader's own memory workload before production adoption.
technique: Multi-agent typed long-term memory with budgeted retrieval

claims.statement: It replaces parametric memory training and unbounded append-and-search history stores with six typed memory agents holding complete records, a provenance hypergraph index, and retrieval under explicit evidence budgets. It costs the operational complexity of running multiple memory agents plus an offline consolidation process (AutoDream), and requires no fine-tuning, working with closed or open models behind APIs. It can fail if the provenance index or retrieval budgets drop relevant records on the reader's specific workloads, since reported gains come from public QA and embodied-task benchmarks that may not transfer.

Most accurate of compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks: 91.4% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on LongMemEval-S (+14.3 points over the strongest baseline), and faster than HyperMem on all five timed benchmarks with AutoDream disabled.
